threadTitle: Things that instantly reveal you just moved here
body: You still call it a 'tube,' not realizing it's just the Overground from here. And good luck finding a proper coffee before 8 am.
Last night on the 59, a guy in a parka argued with a traffic cone for ten minutes. Brixton's nightlife can be as surreal as it gets.

threadTitle: When you knew you were actually living here
body: The first time I saw a stray cat lounging on the counter at my local Späti, I knew Neukölln had stolen my heart.

threadTitle: Things Berlin does that nowhere else does
body: Only in Berlin do you find a 'Kneipe' with a dance floor and a petting zoo next door. Just another Tuesday night in Friedrichshain.

threadTitle: Real signs someone is from here vs just working here
body: You notice the regulars at La Taqueria don’t even look at the menu. They order their super burritos without hesitation, while newbies fumble with their phones.

threadTitle: Muni moments that define this city
body: Saw a pigeon ride the 49 bus today like it was on a city tour. No one batted an eye; just another day in the Tenderloin.

threadTitle: Things tourists get wrong about living here
body: Tourists often miss that the best paella isn't at the beach, but at that tiny corner spot by the park where locals gather for lunch.

threadTitle: How to spot a recent arrival
body: They’re the ones still taking pictures of the local bearded hipster selling bread at La Llibertaria, as if they’ve never seen a sourdough loaf before.

threadTitle: Things that instantly reveal you just moved here
body: I saw a newcomer in a café asking for 'the best place to see the sunrise'—not realizing the view’s blocked by those flats on the corner.
Last night on the 59, a guy asked the driver if he’d seen a chicken. Apparently, it was his pet, and he was dead serious.

threadTitle: When you knew you were actually living here
body: When I caught a glimpse of a group of kids market bartering for old records while the kebab shop blasted 90s Eurodance. Classic Neukölln vibe.

threadTitle: Things Berlin does that nowhere else does
body: Only in Kreuzberg do you find a kebab shop that sells graffiti art alongside your döner. It's the perfect mix of food and culture!

threadTitle: Real signs someone is from here vs just working here
body: You can spot a real local by how they navigate BART delays—eyes roll, deep sigh, then a parking spot search instead of waiting for the next train.

threadTitle: Muni moments that define this city
body: Caught a Muni bus today that took a detour past a block party. Drivers and passengers shared laughs as we crawled by the BBQ smoke and live music.

threadTitle: Things tourists get wrong about living here
body: Tourists often assume Gràcia is all about the parks, but most locals spend evenings crowded into tiny bars, not sprawled outside on benches.

threadTitle: How to spot a recent arrival
body: You can tell a recent arrival by their confusion at the local bus routes — I once saw a couple miss their stop twice while looking at their phones.
